newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Kohl, Kok see EU treaty signed at June summit.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, Kok see EU treaty signed at June summit.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Thursday they were confident the European Union would be able to sign a landmark treaty on EU reform as planned at a June summit in Amsterdam.
"Much remains to be done but there is not the slightest reason to doubt that Amsterdam will be a success," said Kohl.
"The chances of completing the treaty in Amsterdam are very much alive," Kok said.
Kohl met Kok in The Hague on Thursday for talks on a wide range of EU and foreign policy issues. The Netherlands currently holds the EU presidency.
The crisis in Albania was discussed during the talks, also attended by the German and Dutch Foreign Ministers, Klaus Kinkel and Hans van Mierlo.
The European Union has been holding an inter-governmental conference (IGC) to discuss political and institutional reforms and the Dutch hope to present a draft treaty by mid-May.
